Prevention: At the end of the season/harvest collect and bury all fallen fruits in a pit (0.5-1m deep) or tie them in a black plastic bag, then place the bag in the sun to kill potential larvae in the fruits in order to prevent infestation in the next season
Harvest fruits at physiological maturity before they become very ripe and soft which makes it easy for the flies to lay eggs in them
Remove alternate host plants like guava, chillies, citrus, melons, coffee, avocados, wild fruits to reduce pest
Release poultry in the orchard to feed on pupa at the base of plants
Monitoring: Check for adult fruit flies weekly in tree canopies when fruits have set.
C. cosyra looks like a housefly but is yellow with black spots on the back of the chest while
B. invadens looks like a wasp but is brown with a yellow strip on each side of the chest
Check for egg-laying holes ('stings') on the surface of the fruits.
These holes may be indicated by oozing or dry sap
Sample fallen fruits and dissect them for fruit fly larvae which are small white maggots
A catch of 2-3 adult fruit flies per trap per week necessitates control measures (see factsheet on fruit fly traps)
Direct Control: During harvesting collect and bury all fallen fruits in a pit (0.5-1m deep) or tie them in black plastic bags then place the bag in the sun to kill potential larvae in the fruits
Store harvested fruit in cool place or cold storage for 5 days
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
EC at a dilution rate of 1ml / 10 litres of water when fruit flies are noticed
